title: as const and const Type Parameters
summary: Keep literal values precise when TypeScript would otherwise widen them.
nestedConcepts: Use precision where it helps callers

subtopics.title: Preserve literals with as const
subtopics.explanation: `as const` tells TypeScript to keep exact literal values and mark object properties and arrays readonly. For example, `['small', 'large'] as const` becomes a tuple of those two strings instead of a general string array. It changes type checking, not the JavaScript value.

subtopics.title: Preserve literals in generic functions
subtopics.explanation: A `const` type parameter asks TypeScript to infer a precise literal type for an argument passed to a generic function. This can preserve a configuration object’s exact keys and values without requiring `as const` at every call site. Use it when that precision improves the function’s result type.

subtopics.title: Understand readonly inference
subtopics.explanation: Literal-preserving inference often produces readonly properties and tuples, so callers cannot reassign them through that type. This protects the inferred shape during type checking; it does not freeze the object at runtime. Copy or transform the value when the code needs a mutable version.

subtopics.title: Separate type behavior from runtime
subtopics.explanation: `as const` and `const` type parameters affect what TypeScript accepts and infers. They do not change how JavaScript executes or make an object immutable at runtime. Use `Object.freeze()` only when runtime immutability is also required, and remember it has its own limits.

subtopics.title: Use precision where it helps callers
subtopics.explanation: Preserve literal types when callers benefit from a known set of values, such as route names or configuration modes. Avoid forcing narrow types onto ordinary changing data. The goal is useful autocomplete and compile-time checking, not maximum type complexity.

foundations.overview: TypeScript often widens a value such as "ready" to the broader string type. as const keeps literal values narrow and makes object properties readonly. A const type parameter asks a generic function to preserve that precision for its input.
foundations.mentalModel: It is like recording the exact color name instead of writing only “a color.”
foundations.whyItMatters: Precise types improve autocomplete and catch invalid options earlier.

keyTakeaways: as const preserves literal types and readonly structure.
Const type parameters preserve literal inference in generic calls.
Readonly prevents reassignment through that type.
These features affect checking, not runtime behavior.
Use literal precision where values form a meaningful set.

codeLab.title: Preserve Literal Options
codeLab.instructions: Write a helper that keeps the exact tuple values so the allowed status names stay narrow.
codeLab.expectedOutput: The type checker accepts safe values and reports mismatches at compile time.
hints: Keep external values typed as unknown until you check them.
Use a type feature that preserves the exact information you need.
